note: New Zealand, read on Immigration New Zealand's own pages on 2026-10-30. A performer on a run of shows takes the Entertainers Work Visa (the work engine's route), which leads nowhere; to live there the first route is the Accredited Employer Work Visa: an offer of full-time work from an accredited employer, from NZD 1,540, 80% decided within 5 weeks (kept as its time), up to 5 years by the job (3 for skill levels 4 and 5), further AEWVs within the maximum stay, then 12 months away; it is tied to the employer and can lead to a resident visa. The Skilled Migrant Category Resident Visa (an expression of interest, a job or offer from an accredited employer, 55 or younger, English) lets its holder live, work and study indefinitely, from NZD 6,450; after 2 years in a row on a resident visa the Permanent Resident Visa (from NZD 315, 80% within 2 weeks) lifts the travel conditions. Where each is applied for isn't stated on the pages read; 'either' is the game's reading, since the AEWV is applied for online from offshore or onshore, as is a resident visa. Which years count toward citizenship is on the Department of Internal Affairs' citizenship pages, which sit behind a bot check and weren't read, so no route is marked as counting. Australian citizens and permanent residents get a resident visa on arrival; that page sits behind a bot check and wasn't read, so the route isn't written.
